content.overview: Specialist solution preparation follows an approved recipe and work order rather than improvising chemistry. Material identity, recipe version, final volume, sequence, mixing and measured acceptance should all be traceable.

vocabulary.definition: Controlled formulation or work instruction identifying required materials, amounts and sequence.
The completed solution volume against which ingredient additions and concentration calculations are defined.
Decision that a verified finished batch meets the controlled criteria for its intended use.

sections.title: Verify inputs before mixing
sections.body: Confirm source-water identity, material identity, recipe version, units and target final volume before additions begin.

sections.title: Unexpected EC should trigger process verification first
sections.body: Check meter fitness, batch volume, material identity and mixing before adding concentrate simply to chase a number.

sections.title: Chemical safety remains controlled
sections.body: Acids, bases, concentrates and incompatible materials require the applicable PPE, handling and facility procedure. This course does not authorize ad hoc chemical mixing.

workedExamples: A completed batch reads lower EC than expected; verify the meter, final volume, material identity and mixing before changing chemistry.
commonMistakes: Adjusting until the number looks right without preserving the original condition.
Treating source-water changes as irrelevant to the finished batch.
content.practicalApplication: Run a mock batch record from source-water check through material verification, calculated addition, mixing, final volume and acceptance measurements.
content.summary: Batch quality depends on controlled execution and verified measurement, not on chasing a display.
